pagazis: African porters who carried loads on the expedition's marches
pagazi: a single African porter hired to carry loads
bales: large tied bundles of goods, such as cloth, for transport
beads: small pierced glass or stone pieces used as trade goods
ivory: elephant tusk material, traded as a valuable commodity
dhows: small Arab sailing vessels used along the East African coast
frasilah: local unit of weight, roughly thirty-five pounds, used in trade
frasilahs: plural of frasilah, a local unit of weight in trade
gum-copal: hard tree resin traded for making varnish
cocoa-nut: old spelling of coconut, the large tropical palm fruit
orchilla: lichen used to make a purple or red dye
posho: coarse ground maize meal eaten as a basic food
dragoman: interpreter and guide who speaks several languages for travellers
emadar: jemadar, a native officer commanding a small group of soldiers
askari: African soldier or armed guard serving a European employer
caravan: group of travellers and animals or porters moving together with goods
caravans: groups of travellers and porters moving together with goods
canvas: heavy coarse cloth used for tents and sails
sheeting: coarse plain cloth sold in long lengths for trade
portmanteaus: old-fashioned travelling bags that open into two halves
ohammedan: old term for a Muslim, a follower of Islam
half-castes: outdated term for people of mixed European and African descent
half-caste: outdated term for a person of mixed European and African descent
negroes: outdated term for Black people, used here in the book
negro: outdated term for a Black person, used here in the book
honga: tribute or toll paid to local chiefs for passage through territory
usungu: Swahili word for a white foreigner or European
salaams: greetings made with a bowed head, from Arabic salutations
sultan: ruler of a Muslim state, a king or monarch
tribute: payment given by one ruler or people to another for protection
drafts: written orders to pay money, like bills of exchange
custom-house: government office where taxes on imported goods are collected
fowling-piece: light shotgun used for hunting birds
rifle: long gun with a grooved barrel for accurate shooting
powder: gunpowder, the explosive used to fire guns
ammunition: bullets, shot and powder used in firearms
tusks: long curved teeth of an elephant, the source of ivory
hides: animal skins, usually prepared for leather
alcoves: small recesses built into the wall of a room
turban: headwear made by winding a long cloth around the head
councillors: advisers who help a ruler make decisions
verdure: fresh green vegetation covering the land
haggling: arguing back and forth to bargain over a price
mildew: grey or white mould that grows on damp cloth or food
valet: a personal manservant who attends to a gentleman's needs
morrow: the following day, an old word for tomorrow
thereof: of that or of it, an old-fashioned word
wagged: moved quickly from side to side or up and down
gravity: serious and solemn manner or seriousness of a situation
barque: sailing ship with three masts and square sails
quota: a fixed share or allotted number of something
monotone: a single unchanging pitch or dull repetitive sound
chant: a rhythmic sung phrase repeated over and over
bolts: long rolls of cloth sold as one unit
pack-saddles: padded frames strapped on animals to carry loads
equipments: gear and supplies needed for a journey or task
despatched: sent off on a errand or journey
penetrated: reached deep into, gone far inside an unknown area
proprietor: owner of a business or property
flimsy: weak, thin and easily torn or broken
